question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.
sql:
WITH RECURSIVE customer_date_ranges AS (
  SELECT 
    customer_id,
    MIN(txn_date::DATE) as start_date,
    MAX(txn_date::DATE) as end_date
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
customer_dates AS (
  SELECT 
    customer_id,
    start_date,
    end_date,
    start_date as current_date
  FROM customer_date_ranges
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    cd.customer_id,
    cd.start_date,
    cd.end_date,
    cd.current_date + INTERVAL '1 day' as current_date
  FROM customer_dates cd
  JOIN customer_date_ranges c ON cd.customer_id = c.customer_id
  WHERE cd.current_date < c.end_date
),
daily_balances AS (
  SELECT 
    cd.customer_id,
    cd.current_date as txn_date,
    COALESCE(cb.txn_amount, 0) as txn_amount
  FROM customer_dates cd
  LEFT JOIN customer_transactions cb ON cd.customer_id = cb.customer_id AND cd.current_date = cb.txn_date
),
running_balances AS (
  SELECT 
    customer_id,
    txn_date,
    txn_amount,
    SUM(txn_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY txn_date ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) as balance
  FROM daily_balances
),
processed_balances AS (
  SELECT 
    customer_id,
    txn_date,
    MAX(CASE WHEN balance >= 0 THEN balance ELSE 0 END) as daily_balance
  FROM running_balances
  GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
),
monthly_max AS (
  SELECT 
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM txn_date) as month,
    customer_id,
    MAX(daily_balance) as max_daily_balance
  FROM processed_balances
  GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM txn_date), customer_id
)
SELECT 
  month,
  SUM(max_daily_balance) as total_max_balance
FROM monthly_max
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
